item.description:
**Download:** [Leise-2.3.5.zip](https://github.com/ramonfeng/leise/releases/download/v2.3.5/Leise-2.3.5.zip) — quit Leise, then replace the old `Leise.app` in your Applications folder. (First launch after replacing: System Settings → Privacy & Security → "Open Anyway", same as before — [README](https://github.com/ramonfeng/leise#readme).)
## What changed in 2.3.5
- **Updates install themselves now.** When the download finishes, the install prompt appears on its own — the progress bar no longer stalls at 100% waiting for a restart. (One note for this update only: 2.3.5 arrives through the *old* update flow, so if the bar sits at 100%, click "Abbrechen"/"Cancel" and the "Ready to Install" window appears. Every update after this one is smooth.) - **Words no longer stick together in English and German.** "didn'tmake" becomes "didn't make", and a space follows `. ! ? ;` before the next word — both right after dictation and after polishing. - **Leise warns when something else types into your field.** If text from another window or session lands in the middle of your dictation, a warning appears instead of the text silently mixing in. Your dictated text is never re-typed or overwritten. - **A recording pill of Leise's own.** The capsule at the bottom is redesigned — wider, nine bars, its own stop/check icons, Liquid Glass on macOS 26 — and the waveform motion is tuned against measured dynamics. - **German says Du everywhere.** The last 27 Sie strings joined the rest. - **Feedback is one click away.** Settings → Feedback drafts a mail to feedback@leiseapp.com carrying only the app version, the macOS version and the interface language. - **Chinese dictation with English passages decodes more calmly.** English-language windows in the zh/de route fall back to automatic detection instead of being forced.
## The essentials (unchanged)
**Apple Silicon only** (M1 or newer) · **macOS 14.4+** (on-device polishing additionally needs a newer macOS with Apple Intelligence; without it Leise Engine uses its bundled model) · about **5–7 GB free disk** (app + speech models; 2.1 GB less when your Mac's built-in intelligence does the polishing).
A 100 % local dictation app for macOS. Your audio and your transcripts never leave your Mac; it works with the network off.
